interpretation: A required checkpoint creates a real bidirectional plan reversal: both policy-first and query-first are confidence-set singleton winners in the frozen matrix.
Width and policy selectivity affect the crossover at q=0.13 and q=0.16.

The fitted threshold 0.160000001 is just above the largest measured q=0.16, so within this matrix it degenerates to the fixed query-first baseline; its 34/37 accuracy mainly reflects label imbalance rather than a learned internal switching boundary.
The pre-registered admission rule therefore does not justify training a more complex multifactor optimizer for this isolated two-candidate family.
The eleven inconclusive scenarios are not relabelled as wins for either candidate.
decision: Stop complex model development for this isolated required-checkpoint two-candidate family. Use governance feasibility to determine the legal candidate set and retain fixed query-first as the strongest simple development baseline for this matrix; do not promote the degenerate 0.16 threshold to a validated optimizer. Continue paper work on the full legal-plan enumerator, governance overhead, semantic correctness, and broader query families rather than weakening this gate.
